What add_lmed_v20260924() does

Source: vignettes/lmed-v20260924.Rmd
lmed-v20260924.Rmd

add_lmed_v20260924() takes a table of dispensed prescriptions and a person-week skeleton. It writes menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) exposure columns and two person-level exclusion columns onto the skeleton. Exposure here means dispensed supply, assumed used. The function reads the dispensed quantity and, for two strength-keyed rules, the strength. It reads no adherence and no indication. It runs six steps, in this order:

  1. It looks each product name up in a shipped product table. The table gives the product’s MHT category, and whether the study removes its holders.
  2. It turns each prescription into a closed interval of ISO weeks.
  3. It marks each person-week with the categories in force that week.
  4. It resolves the categories into one treatment level per week, under each of four approaches.
  5. It derives the rd_approach* exposure variables from those levels.
  6. It flags every week of a person whose supplied prescriptions include a product the table marks for removal.

The product table is product_table_20260924.xlsx. The duration rules and the approach rules come from the codebook dataDictionary20260924.xlsx. Both workbooks are dated 2026-09-24 and ship with the package. The function reads no other workbook. The tables below are read from the two files when the vignette builds.

Approach 4 is new in this function. It splits systemic oestrogen by its route and by the type of progestogen dispensed with it. Every helper that reads a workbook, directly or through another helper, has a 2026-09-24 copy. The exposure layer also has a copy, because it writes the two rd_approach4 columns. Every other helper is an older dated one, called unchanged. Section 1 states the changes against add_lmed_v20260922(). Section 3 verifies on the fixture that the two functions agree in every column that both write. The vignette lmed-v20260922 stays as the record of that frozen version.

The function’s arguments, the columns it owns and the conditions it rejects are in ?add_lmed_v20260924 and ?add_lmed_v20260922.

product_table <- system.file("2023-mht", "product_table_20260924.xlsx", package = "mht")
codebook <- system.file("2023-mht", "dataDictionary20260924.xlsx", package = "mht")

# Every product row of a product table, from every sheet but README.
read_product_rows <- function(path) {
  sheets <- setdiff(readxl::excel_sheets(path), "README")
  return(rbindlist(
    lapply(sheets, function(s) {
      setDT(suppressMessages(readxl::read_excel(path, sheet = s, col_types = "text")))
    }),
    use.names = TRUE,
    fill = TRUE
  ))
}
setdiff(readxl::excel_sheets(product_table), "README")
#> [1] "G"     "other"
ptab <- read_product_rows(product_table)
sheet_atc <- lapply(c(G = "G", other = "other"), function(s) {
  readxl::read_excel(product_table, sheet = s, col_types = "text")$atc
})
lengths(sheet_atc)
#>     G other 
#>   182  2425
stopifnot(
  all(sheet_atc$G %like% "^G0[23]"), !any(sheet_atc$other %like% "^G0[23]"),
  sum(lengths(sheet_atc)) == nrow(ptab)
)
groups <- setDT(readxl::read_excel(codebook, sheet = "MHT_groups", col_types = "text"))
groups <- groups[!is.na(Preparatnamn)]

1. Products and categories

How a product name is looked up

The function reduces the register’s product name to its ASCII letters, then lowercases it. Estradot 25, Estradot® and Estradot all become estradot. It then looks that key up in the product table, on an exact match. Extra digits, spaces and symbols disappear in the reduction, so they still match. Extra letters do not: estradotmatrix would match no key. The table holds one row per raw register name, so several rows can share one key. Rows that share a key MUST agree on the category, on the exclusion flag and on its reason. The function errors where they do not.

key_of(c("Estradot 25", "Estradot®", "Estradot", "Estradot Matrix"))
#> [1] "estradot"       "estradot"       "estradot"       "estradotmatrix"
stopifnot(
  all(key_of(c("Estradot 25", "Estradot®", "Estradot")) == "estradot"),
  "estradot" %chin% ptab$produkt_clean,
  !key_of("Estradot Matrix") %chin% ptab$produkt_clean
)
spellings <- lapply(c("Estradot 25", "Estradot®", "Estradot"), function(p) run_toy(rx(p, 1, 10)))
stopifnot(
  all(spellings[[1]]$A1[1:10]),
  identical(spellings[[1]], spellings[[2]]),
  identical(spellings[[1]], spellings[[3]])
)
msg <- error_of(run_toy(rx("Estradot Matrix", 1, 10)))
msg
#> [1] "1 delivered products have no row in the product table: Estradot Matrix. A product with no row would read as no MHT, so the woman would enter as an unexposed control. Add each one to the table, as a category or as notmht, before the run."
stopifnot(startsWith(msg, "1 delivered products have no row"))

The chunk also runs the function on each spelling. The three runs give the same columns, and Estradot Matrix stops the run.

A product name with no row is an error. The function checks the whole prescription table before it restricts to the people in the skeleton. A product held only by people outside the cohort therefore still needs a row. A product nobody has ruled on would otherwise read as no MHT, and its holder would enter as an unexposed control. The run stops with an error that names up to five such products. This table is frozen. A missing row goes into a new dated table, which a new dated function reads.

The chunk below passes six unknown product names, all held by person 99, who is not in the skeleton. The function stops, names five of the six, and writes no column.

outside <- data.table(
  lopnr = 99L, produkt = paste("Unknown product", 1:6), edatum = monday, fddd = 28, lnmn = NA_character_
)
skel <- toy_skeleton()
msg <- error_of(add_lmed_v20260924(skel, rbind(rx("Divigel", 1, 10), outside), verbose = FALSE))
msg
#> [1] "6 delivered products have no row in the product table: Unknown product 1 | Unknown product 2 | Unknown product 3 | Unknown product 4 | Unknown product 5. A product with no row would read as no MHT, so the woman would enter as an unexposed control. Add each one to the table, as a category or as notmht, before the run."
stopifnot(
  startsWith(msg, "6 delivered products have no row"),
  lengths(regmatches(msg, gregexpr("Unknown product", msg))) == 5L,
  identical(names(skel), c("id", "isoyearweek", "week"))
)

notmht in the table is a recorded decision that the product is not MHT. A prescription of such a product contributes nothing, and no warning names it.

The reader validates four things. A category MUST be one the person-week grid materialises, one the 2026-08-28 classifier returns, or notmht. The exclusion cell MUST read TRUE or FALSE. The key MUST equal the raw name reduced, because the function recomputes it. Rows sharing a key MUST agree, as above. No other cell is checked. The chunk below breaks one row of the table in each of the first three ways, and passes each broken table to the function’s validator. The intact table passes.

validate <- mht:::lmed_validate_product_table_v20260902
i <- which(ptab$classification == "A1")[1]
broken <- list(
  category = copy(ptab)[i, classification := "Al"],
  flag = copy(ptab)[i, exclude_entire_person := "yes"],
  key = copy(ptab)[i, produkt_clean := "estradot"]
)
invalid <- vapply(broken, function(x) error_of(validate(x)), "")
invalid
#>                                                                                                                                                                                                          category 
#> "1 table rows carry a classification that is neither a materialised category nor notmht: Al. A category the person-week grid never materialises reaches no approach rule, so the person would read as untreated." 
#>                                                                                                                                                                                                              flag 
#>                                                                       "the exclude_entire_person column carries YES. Only TRUE and FALSE are read. Any other value would silently keep the person in the cohort." 
#>                                                                                                                                                                                                               key 
#>                                                                                                                                  "1 table rows carry a produkt_clean that is not produkt_raw normalised: Climara"
stopifnot(
  grepl("neither a materialised category nor notmht", invalid[["category"]]),
  grepl("exclude_entire_person column carries YES", invalid[["flag"]]),
  grepl("not produkt_raw normalised", invalid[["key"]]),
  is.na(error_of(validate(copy(ptab))))
)

The categories

The table names 33 categories, each with at least one product. A category is one letter for the drug group and one number for a subgroup: the route, the progestogen or the regimen. The table below lists every product that reaches each category. The meaning column is the product table’s own English translation of the codebook’s group and route cells, shown without the table’s parenthetical notes. The route is the codebook’s. The lookup reads the product name only, and never checks the route dispensed.

legend <- ptab[classification != "notmht",
  .(
    meaning = paste(unique(sub(" \\(.*\\)$", "", classification_meaning)), collapse = " | "),
    products = paste(unique(produkt_raw), collapse = ", ")
  ),
  keyby = .(category = classification)
]
legend <- legend[order(substr(category, 1, 1), as.integer(substring(category, 2)))]
knitr::kable(legend)

The letter groups the drug. A is oestrogen alone. B is oestrogen with a progestogen in one product. C is a progestogen alone. D, E and I are contraceptive progestogens. F is tibolone, G is a tissue-selective oestrogen complex and H is an androgen. The codebook counts A3, A4 and A5 as local treatment, although A5 is a peroral oestriol. No approach rule treats one of the three as MHT exposure.

What changed against the 2026-09-22 function

The product table is product_table_20260922.xlsx with one note cell reworded. No column that the function reads changes. The chunk compares every cell of every sheet of the two tables.

read_sheets <- function(path) {
  sheets <- readxl::excel_sheets(path)
  return(setNames(lapply(sheets, function(s) {
    readxl::read_excel(path, sheet = s, col_types = "text", .name_repair = "unique_quiet")
  }), sheets))
}
pt_now <- read_sheets(product_table)
pt_before <- read_sheets(system.file("2023-mht", "product_table_20260922.xlsx", package = "mht"))
drop_note <- function(x) lapply(x, function(d) d[setdiff(names(d), "note")])
notes <- function(x) unlist(lapply(x, `[[`, "note"), use.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(
  identical(lapply(pt_now, names), lapply(pt_before, names)),
  identical(drop_note(pt_now), drop_note(pt_before)),
  sum(!mapply(identical, notes(pt_now), notes(pt_before))) == 1L
)

The codebook is dataDictionary20260922.xlsx with 47 approach 4 rules added to the post_grouping sheet, after the 88 rules of approaches 1 to 3. Every other sheet is unchanged, and so is every rule of approaches 1 to 3. The chunk reads the rules with the function’s own reader.

codebook_before <- system.file("2023-mht", "dataDictionary20260922.xlsx", package = "mht")
stopifnot(identical(readxl::excel_sheets(codebook), readxl::excel_sheets(codebook_before)))
for (s in setdiff(readxl::excel_sheets(codebook), "post_grouping")) {
  stopifnot(identical(
    suppressMessages(readxl::read_excel(codebook, sheet = s, col_types = "text")),
    suppressMessages(readxl::read_excel(codebook_before, sheet = s, col_types = "text"))
  ))
}
rules <- mht:::lmed_read_approach_rules_v20260924()
rules_before <- mht:::lmed_read_approach_rules_v20260922()
approach_of <- vapply(rules, function(r) as.character(r$approach), "")
table(approach_of)
#> approach_of
#>  1  2  3  4 
#> 19 19 50 47
raw_pg <- function(path) {
  x <- setDT(suppressMessages(readxl::read_excel(path, sheet = "post_grouping", col_types = "text")))
  return(x[!is.na(approach)])
}
pg_now <- raw_pg(codebook)
pg_old <- raw_pg(codebook_before)
stopifnot(
  identical(pg_now[seq_len(nrow(pg_old))], pg_old),
  all(pg_now[-seq_len(nrow(pg_old)), approach] == "4")
)
stopifnot(
  length(rules_before) == 88L,
  length(rules) == 135L,
  sum(approach_of == "4") == 47L,
  identical(rules[approach_of != "4"], rules_before)
)

The function writes three columns that add_lmed_v20260922() does not: approach4, rd_approach4_single and rd_approach4_multiple. Section 3 checks that every other column is identical.

Categories that never change exposure

Three categories can be classified and still move no exposure variable: A7, G1 and H1. A fourth, D4, is a column that no product reaches. A3, A4 and A5 are read only by the inert reference-level rules of section 4, so they move nothing either. Approach 4 reads no category that approaches 1 to 3 do not already read.

pg <- setDT(suppressMessages(
  readxl::read_excel(codebook, sheet = "post_grouping", col_types = "text")
))
pg <- pg[!is.na(approach)]
ex_cols <- grep("^doesnotinclude", names(pg), value = TRUE)
read_by <- function(x) cat_order(na.omit(unlist(x[, c("includes1", "includes2", ex_cols), with = FALSE])))
read <- read_by(pg)
read
#>  [1] "A1"  "A2"  "A3"  "A4"  "A5"  "A6"  "B1"  "B2"  "B3"  "B4"  "B5"  "B6" 
#> [13] "B7"  "B8"  "B9"  "B10" "B11" "B12" "C1"  "C2"  "C3"  "C4"  "C5"  "D1" 
#> [25] "D2"  "D3"  "E1"  "F1"  "I1"  "I2"
stopifnot(identical(read, read_by(pg[approach != "4"])), all(read_by(pg[approach == "4"]) %in% read))
  • A7 is the injected oestrogens. The grid carries an A7 column, and no approach rule names it. Section 4 shows a week of A7 alone.
  • G1 is Duavive alone, and Duavive counts as no MHT. The table gives it G1, and the person-week grid has no G1 column, so no rule can read it.
  • H1 is the androgens. The grid carries an H1 column, and no approach rule names it.
  • D4 appears nowhere in the codebook. The grid carries a D4 column that is FALSE in every week, and no rule names it.

Products whose holders the study removes

The table flags a product with exclude_entire_person. The flag is separate from the category: a flagged product keeps its category, and its category column still marks each week it covers. Every A7 product is flagged, so every woman with an A7 dispensing is flagged. Section 6 states what the function does with the flag.

ptab[exclude_entire_person == "TRUE", .(produkt_raw, classification, exclusion_reason)]
#>                              produkt_raw classification
#>                                   <char>         <char>
#> 1:                           Delestrogen             A7
#> 2:                    Estradiol Valerate             A7
#> 3:                             Neofollin             A7
#> 4:                             Cyclogest             C1
#> 5: Extempore ATC-kod G03DA04 Progesteron             C1
#> 6:    Lugesteron 100 mg -kapseli, pehmeä             C1
#> 7:    Lugesteron 200 mg -kapseli, pehmeä             C1
#> 8:                              Prolutex             C2
#> 9:       Prolutex 25 mg Injektionslösung             C2
#>                            exclusion_reason
#>                                      <char>
#> 1:        possible gender-affirming therapy
#> 2:        possible gender-affirming therapy
#> 3:        possible gender-affirming therapy
#> 4:   private prescribing without monitoring
#> 5:   private prescribing without monitoring
#> 6:   private prescribing without monitoring
#> 7:   private prescribing without monitoring
#> 8: possible gender-affirming therapy or IVF
#> 9: possible gender-affirming therapy or IVF
stopifnot(all(ptab[classification == "A7", exclude_entire_person] == "TRUE"))

2. From a prescription to an interval

The layer reads five columns of the prescription table: the person identifier, produkt, edatum, fddd, and lnmn where a strength-keyed rule needs it. It reads fddd as a number of days, rounded to a whole day with round(), unless a codebook rule says otherwise.

Four steps run, in this order:

  1. Look the product up, as in section 1.
  2. Overwrite fddd with the codebook’s fixed duration, for the products that carry one.
  3. Drop every prescription with no category, no dispensing date, or no positive duration.
  4. Read the strength from lnmn, and apply the whole-months rules.

Step 2 runs before step 3 because an implant carries no useful dispensed quantity, and the fixed duration supplies one. Step 4 runs after step 3 because a prescription with no duration has no interval at any strength. If step 4 ran first, a missing lnmn on such a row would be an error, although step 3 drops the row.

The duration rules come from the codebook’s MHT_groups sheet, and they are matched by prefix, not by exact key. A rule applies where its codebook name is a prefix of the reduced product name, and the longest such name wins. Utrogestan 100mg Capsules takes the Utrogestan rule. An alias in the duration layer gives Utrogest and Gepretix the Utrogestan rules. Their categories come from the table, where all three are C1. The category lookup and the duration rule are chosen independently, and nothing checks that the rule’s codebook subgroup agrees with the table’s category.

The interval is closed. A prescription dispensed on edatum for d days covers edatum to edatum + d - 1. Both ends convert to an ISO week with cstime::date_to_isoyearweek_c(). Each prescription gets its own interval. Overlapping intervals of one category are unioned, and supply left over at a refill is not carried forward.

The chunk below shows the week boundaries. One day of Divigel on a Sunday marks one week, and two days from that Sunday mark two. A 10-week supply refilled in week 9 for 4 weeks covers weeks 1 to 12, the union of the two intervals. A 10-week supply dispensed 4 weeks before the skeleton starts covers weeks 1 to 6 of it, and the episode starts in week 1.

on_sunday <- function(fddd) data.table(lopnr = 1L, produkt = "Divigel", edatum = monday + 6L, fddd = fddd, lnmn = NA_character_)
one_day <- run_toy(on_sunday(1))
two_days <- run_toy(on_sunday(2))
refill <- run_toy(rbind(rx("Divigel", 1, 10), rx("Divigel", 9, 4)))
early <- run_toy(rx("Divigel", -3, 10))
stopifnot(
  identical(which(one_day$A1), 1L),
  identical(which(two_days$A1), 1:2),
  identical(which(refill$A1), 1:12),
  identical(which(early$A1), 1:6),
  identical(early$approach1[1:7], rep(c("systemic_mht", "local_or_none_mht"), c(6L, 1L)))
)

Fixed durations 

knitr::kable(groups[!is.na(FDDD), .(Preparatnamn, Subgrupp, FDDD)])
Preparatnamn Subgrupp FDDD
Jadelle D3 1680
Jaydess E1 1008
Kyleena E1 1680
Levosert E1 1680
Levosertone E1 1680
Mirena E1 1680 
stopifnot(nrow(groups[!is.na(FDDD)]) == 6L, groups[Preparatnamn == "Jadelle", FDDD] == "1680")

1680 days is five years of twelve 28-day months, which is 240 weeks. 1008 days is three years of the same months, which is 144 weeks. Jaydess is the one product whose fixed duration differs from the rest of its category. The function reads no removal or replacement date, so a device’s interval runs its full length or ends with follow-up. The chunk dispenses each hormonal IUD (E1) once, with fddd = 1, and counts the weeks its E1 column marks.

iud <- ptab[classification == "E1", unique(produkt_raw)]
iud_days <- groups[Preparatnamn %in% iud, .(produkt = Preparatnamn, days = as.numeric(FDDD))]
iud_days[, weeks := vapply(produkt, function(p) sum(run_toy(rx(p, 1, fddd = 1), 250L)$E1), integer(1))]
iud_days
#>        produkt  days weeks
#>         <char> <num> <int>
#> 1:     Jaydess  1008   144
#> 2:     Kyleena  1680   240
#> 3:    Levosert  1680   240
#> 4: Levosertone  1680   240
#> 5:      Mirena  1680   240
stopifnot(
  setequal(iud_days$produkt, iud),
  all(iud_days$weeks == iud_days$days / 7),
  identical(iud_days[days == 1008, produkt], "Jaydess"),
  setequal(iud_days[days == 1680, produkt], setdiff(iud, "Jaydess"))
)

Whole months for sparse progestogens

A sequential progestogen is taken on some days of each month. Its fddd counts the days of supply, and a sparse supply covers more calendar time than it has days. For each such product the codebook gives minimum_monthly_dose, the days of supply that make one treatment month, and minimum_months, the months a prescription must reach.

knitr::kable(groups[
  !is.na(minimum_monthly_dose),
  .(Preparatnamn, Subgrupp, minimum_monthly_dose, minimum_months, strength_mg_min, strength_mg_max)
])
Preparatnamn Subgrupp minimum_monthly_dose minimum_months strength_mg_min strength_mg_max
Crinone C1 12 1 NA NA
Cyclogest C1 3.33 3 NA NA
Lutinus C1 8 3 NA NA
Utrogestan C1 28 1 NA 150
Utrogestan C1 12 1 150 NA
Progesteron MIC APL C1 3.33 3 NA NA
Desogestrel C3 4 3 NA NA
Cerazette C3 4 3 NA NA
Azalia C3 4 3 NA NA
Gestrina C3 4 3 NA NA
Velavel C3 4 3 NA NA
Vinelle C3 4 3 NA NA
Zarelle C3 4 3 NA NA
Primolut-Nor C4 4.66 3 NA NA
Provera C4 4 3 NA NA
Orgametril C4 4 3 NA NA
Gestapuran C4 4 3 NA NA
Duphaston C5 12 1 NA NA

The rule rewrites fddd in three steps:

  1. months = floor(fddd / minimum_monthly_dose).
  2. If months < minimum_months, the duration is zero and the prescription is dropped.
  3. Otherwise fddd = months * 28.

The function uses a 28-day month, which is four whole weeks. The result rounds down.

Two Utrogestan rules are keyed on strength. strength_mg_min is inclusive and strength_mg_max is exclusive, so the pair NA, 150 and 150, NA covers every strength once. The strength comes from lnmn, the register’s full product name, which carries the dosage form and the strength. The strength is the last number in lnmn followed by mg, with a comma read as a decimal point. A number followed by mg/ is a concentration and does not count. As soon as a strength-keyed product survives step 3, lnmn is required. A surviving row of it with no readable strength is an error.

The chunk below drives the duration layer with one row per case. The layer is an internal function, so the chunk calls it directly, with the product table that the function reads.

u <- groups[Preparatnamn == "Utrogestan"]
u[, .(Preparatnamn, minimum_monthly_dose, strength_mg_min, strength_mg_max)]
#>    Preparatnamn minimum_monthly_dose strength_mg_min strength_mg_max
#>          <char>               <char>          <char>          <char>
#> 1:   Utrogestan                   28            <NA>             150
#> 2:   Utrogestan                   12             150            <NA>
stopifnot(
  nrow(u) == 2L,
  nrow(u[is.na(strength_mg_min) & strength_mg_max == "150"]) == 1L,
  nrow(u[strength_mg_min == "150" & is.na(strength_mg_max)]) == 1L
)
cases <- data.table(
  produkt = c("Divigel", "Cerazette", "Provera", "Provera", "Utrogestan", "Utrogestan", "Utrogestan",
              "Utrogestan 100mg Capsules", "Utrogest", "Gepretix", "Mirena", "Jaydess",
              "Divigel", "Divigel", "Mirena"),
  lnmn = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, "Utrogestan, kapsel, mjuk 100 mg", "Utrogestan, kapsel, mjuk 150 mg",
           "Utrogestan, kapsel, mjuk 200 mg", "Utrogestan, kapsel, mjuk 100 mg",
           "Utrogest, kapsel, mjuk 100 mg", "Gepretix, kapsel, mjuk 100 mg", NA, NA, NA, NA, NA),
  edatum = as.Date("2020-01-06"),
  fddd = c(90, 28, 28, 8, 30, 30, 30, 30, 30, 30, 1, 1, NA, 90, NA)
)
cases[, lopnr := seq_len(.N)]
cases[14, edatum := NA]
warned <- character(0)
intervals <- withCallingHandlers(
  mht:::lmed_durations_v20260924(cases, mht:::lmed_read_product_table_v20260924(), verbose = FALSE),
  warning = function(w) {
    warned <<- c(warned, conditionMessage(w))
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
)
intervals[, .(case = lopnr, produkt, lnmn, duration_days, start_isoyearweek, stop_isoyearweek)]
#>      case                   produkt                            lnmn
#>     <int>                    <char>                          <char>
#>  1:     1                   Divigel                            <NA>
#>  2:     2                 Cerazette                            <NA>
#>  3:     3                   Provera                            <NA>
#>  4:     5                Utrogestan Utrogestan, kapsel, mjuk 100 mg
#>  5:     6                Utrogestan Utrogestan, kapsel, mjuk 150 mg
#>  6:     7                Utrogestan Utrogestan, kapsel, mjuk 200 mg
#>  7:     8 Utrogestan 100mg Capsules Utrogestan, kapsel, mjuk 100 mg
#>  8:     9                  Utrogest   Utrogest, kapsel, mjuk 100 mg
#>  9:    10                  Gepretix   Gepretix, kapsel, mjuk 100 mg
#> 10:    11                    Mirena                            <NA>
#> 11:    12                   Jaydess                            <NA>
#> 12:    15                    Mirena                            <NA>
#>     duration_days start_isoyearweek stop_isoyearweek
#>             <num>            <char>           <char>
#>  1:            90           2020-02          2020-14
#>  2:           196           2020-02          2020-29
#>  3:           196           2020-02          2020-29
#>  4:            28           2020-02          2020-05
#>  5:            56           2020-02          2020-09
#>  6:            56           2020-02          2020-09
#>  7:            28           2020-02          2020-05
#>  8:            28           2020-02          2020-05
#>  9:            28           2020-02          2020-05
#> 10:          1680           2020-02          2024-32
#> 11:          1008           2020-02          2022-40
#> 12:          1680           2020-02          2024-32
warned
#> [1] "3 of 15 classified prescriptions dropped: 1 with no duration, 1 with a duration that is no positive number of days, 1 with no dispensing date"
days <- intervals[match(seq_len(nrow(cases)), lopnr), duration_days]
stopifnot(
  identical(as.numeric(days), c(90, 196, 196, NA, 28, 56, 56, 28, 28, 28, 1680, 1008, NA, NA, 1680)),
  identical(warned, paste(
    "3 of 15 classified prescriptions dropped: 1 with no duration,",
    "1 with a duration that is no positive number of days, 1 with no dispensing date"
  ))
)

Divigel has no rule and keeps 90 days. Cerazette and Provera at 28 days of supply reach seven months, which is 196 days. Provera at 8 days of supply reaches two months. The rule needs three, so the prescription is dropped and the warning reports it. Utrogestan 100 mg needs 28 days of supply per month and gets one month. Utrogestan 150 mg and 200 mg take the other rule, which needs 12, and get two. The names Utrogestan 100mg Capsules, Utrogest and Gepretix take the Utrogestan rules. Mirena and Jaydess take their fixed durations regardless of fddd, and so does a Mirena with no fddd. A Divigel with no fddd and a Divigel with no dispensing date are dropped, and the warning counts them.

Dropped prescriptions

A prescription of a notmht product reaches no category and is dropped silently. Every other drop is counted in one aggregate warning, under three causes:

  • no dispensing date
  • no duration
  • a duration that is no positive number of days, which includes a whole-months result of zero

Outside the six fixed-duration products, a missing fddd is never imputed.

3. Person-weeks

The skeleton MUST hold each person’s ISO weeks once each, with no gap between the first and the last. Gap bridging and the three-year rule both count rows, and a row is one elapsed week only under that condition. The function errors otherwise, before it writes anything. The chunk below drops week 5 from a toy skeleton.

gapped <- toy_skeleton()[-5]
error_of(add_lmed_v20260924(gapped, rx("Divigel", 1, 10), verbose = FALSE))
#> [1] "the check fails for 1 of 1 persons. Each person must hold each ISO week once, consecutively. id 1 has 39 rows, 39 distinct weeks, spanning 40 weeks"
stopifnot(
  grepl("id 1 has 39 rows, 39 distinct weeks, spanning 40 weeks",
        error_of(add_lmed_v20260924(gapped, rx("Divigel", 1, 10), verbose = FALSE)), fixed = TRUE),
  identical(names(gapped), c("id", "isoyearweek", "week"))
)

Each of the 33 grid categories gets one logical column. G1 is discarded before this step, and D4 is a column that no product reaches. A week is TRUE for a category where any interval of that category includes at least one day of the week. One day of supply on a Sunday marks that week. The same day plus the Monday marks two weeks. An episode already running at a person’s first week is clipped: it reads as starting in that week. The function counts observed weeks and reads no week before the first one.

The synthetic fixtures show the result. fake_lmed_2026 holds one Utrogestan user, so lnmn is set for those rows first. It also carries one product name, Paracetamol, that has no row in the product table, so the chunk drops that row. The function would stop on it otherwise. Person 18 held only that row, so the chunk gives her one Estradiol Valerate dispensing instead.

skeleton <- copy(fake_skeleton_mht)
lmed <- copy(fake_lmed_2026)
lmed[, lnmn := NA_character_]
lmed[produkt == "Utrogestan", lnmn := UTROGESTAN]
lmed <- lmed[produkt != "Paracetamol"]
lmed <- rbind(lmed, data.table(
  lopnr = 18L,
  produkt = "Estradiol Valerate",
  edatum = as.Date("2016-05-23"),
  fddd = 28,
  lnmn = NA_character_
))
add_lmed_v20260924(skeleton, lmed, verbose = FALSE)
#> Warning: 1 of 128 classified prescriptions dropped: 0 with no duration, 1 with
#> a duration that is no positive number of days, 0 with no dispensing date
categories <- grep("^[A-I][0-9]+$", names(skeleton), value = TRUE)
categories
#>  [1] "A1"  "A2"  "A3"  "A4"  "A5"  "A6"  "A7"  "B1"  "B2"  "B3"  "B4"  "B5" 
#> [13] "B6"  "B7"  "B8"  "B9"  "B10" "B11" "B12" "C1"  "C2"  "C3"  "C4"  "C5" 
#> [25] "D1"  "D2"  "D3"  "D4"  "E1"  "F1"  "H1"  "I1"  "I2"
skeleton[, lapply(.SD, sum), .SDcols = categories][, .SD, .SDcols = function(x) x > 0]
#>       A1    A2    A3    A4    A5    A6    A7    B1    B2    B3    B4    B5
#>    <int> <int> <int> <int> <int> <int> <int> <int> <int> <int> <int> <int>
#> 1:   724   104   127     5     5     4     8     4     5     5     5     5
#>       B6    B7    B8    B9   B11    C1    C3    C4    D2    D3    E1    F1
#>    <int> <int> <int> <int> <int> <int> <int> <int> <int> <int> <int> <int>
#> 1:     4     5     5     4     5    76   178    29     4   240   385     5
#>       H1    I1    I2
#>    <int> <int> <int>
#> 1:     5     5     5

The grid materialises 33 categories. Three of them, A7, D4 and H1, are read by no approach rule:

setdiff(categories, read)
#> [1] "A7" "D4" "H1"
stopifnot(length(categories) == 33L, identical(setdiff(categories, read), c("A7", "D4", "H1")))

Agreement with the 2026-09-22 function

The chunk below runs add_lmed_v20260922() on the same input. The 2026-09-24 function writes the three approach 4 columns in addition. Every other column is identical, for every person.

older <- copy(fake_skeleton_mht)
add_lmed_v20260922(older, lmed, verbose = FALSE)
#> Warning: 1 of 128 classified prescriptions dropped: 0 with no duration, 1 with
#> a duration that is no positive number of days, 0 with no dispensing date
added <- setdiff(names(skeleton), names(older))
added
#> [1] "approach4"             "rd_approach4_single"   "rd_approach4_multiple"
stopifnot(
  identical(added, c("approach4", "rd_approach4_single", "rd_approach4_multiple")),
  identical(setdiff(names(skeleton), added), names(older)),
  identical(skeleton[, names(older), with = FALSE], older)
)

The skeleton must be weekly

swereg::create_skeleton() writes one annual row per person per year before the weekly rows. An annual row holds is_isoyear = TRUE and an isoyearweek that is no ISO week:

id isoyearweek is_isoyear
1 1946-** TRUE
1 2015-02 FALSE

The function stops on the annual row, before it writes anything:

annual <- rbind(data.table(id = 1L, isoyearweek = "1946-**", week = 0L), toy_skeleton())
msg <- error_of(add_lmed_v20260924(annual, rx("Divigel", 1, 10), verbose = FALSE))
msg
#> [1] "skeleton$isoyearweek holds a value that is no ISO week: 1946-**"
stopifnot(grepl("no ISO week: 1946-**", msg, fixed = TRUE), identical(names(annual), c("id", "isoyearweek", "week")))

Pass the weekly rows only, and fill the annual rows in the caller:

weekly <- skeleton[is_isoyear == FALSE]
add_lmed_v20260924(weekly, lmed)

The subset is a new data.table, so the function writes its columns there.

4. From categories to a treatment level

The post_grouping sheet defines four approaches. Each approach is a set of rules. A rule names one treatment variable, the categories a week must carry, and the categories it must not carry. The rule lights its variable in every week that carries all of the first set and none of the second. Several rules can name one variable, and each lights it on its own.

The tables below compress the rules that name at least one category. alone lists the categories that light the variable on their own. pairs lists the combinations that light it, written as oestrogens + partners. Every oestrogen listed pairs with every partner listed. The chunk asserts that the pairs are exactly that cross, with no pair missing and none repeated. excludes lists the categories a week must not carry. Every rule of one variable carries the same excludes, and the chunk asserts that too.

pg[, excludes := apply(.SD, 1, function(r) paste(cat_order(r[!is.na(r)]), collapse = " ")),
  .SDcols = ex_cols]
rule_table <- function(a) {
  x <- pg[approach == a & !is.na(includes1)]
  out <- x[, {
    alone <- includes1[is.na(includes2)]
    p1 <- includes1[!is.na(includes2)]
    p2 <- includes2[!is.na(includes2)]
    seen <- paste(p1, p2)
    cross <- as.vector(outer(unique(p1), unique(p2), paste))
    stopifnot(anyDuplicated(seen) == 0L, setequal(seen, cross))
    stopifnot(length(unique(excludes)) == 1L)
    .(
      rules = .N,
      alone = paste(cat_order(alone), collapse = " "),
      pairs = if (length(p1) == 0L) "" else
        paste(paste(cat_order(p1), collapse = "/"), "+", paste(cat_order(p2), collapse = "/")),
      excludes = paste(unique(excludes[nzchar(excludes)]), collapse = " | ")
    )
  }, keyby = variable]
  return(out[order(variable == "local_or_none_mht", variable)])
}
# The categories that light variable `v` of approach `a` alone, and the two
# sides of its pair rules.
alone_in <- function(a, v) cat_order(pg[approach == a & variable == v & !is.na(includes1) & is.na(includes2), includes1])
pair_in <- function(a, v, col) cat_order(na.omit(pg[approach == a & variable == v & !is.na(includes2)][[col]]))
excludes_in <- function(a, v) unique(pg[approach == a & variable == v & !is.na(includes1), excludes])
# The combination products by route, and the partner categories, from the product table and the grid.
b_route <- unique(ptab[classification %like% "^B", .(category = classification, route)])
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(b_route$category))
b_oral <- cat_order(b_route[route == "oral", category])
b_patch <- cat_order(b_route[route == "transdermal", category])
partners_all <- setdiff(grep("^[CDEI]", categories, value = TRUE), "D4")
b_oral
#>  [1] "B2"  "B3"  "B4"  "B5"  "B6"  "B8"  "B9"  "B10" "B11" "B12"
b_patch
#> [1] "B1" "B7"
partners_all
#>  [1] "C1" "C2" "C3" "C4" "C5" "D1" "D2" "D3" "E1" "I1" "I2"
stopifnot(setequal(c(b_oral, b_patch), b_route$category), length(b_patch) == 2L, length(b_oral) == 10L)

Approach 1: any systemic MHT 

knitr::kable(rule_table("1"))
variable rules alone pairs excludes
systemic_mht 15 A1 A2 A6 B1 B2 B3 B4 B5 B6 B7 B8 B9 B10 B11 B12
tibolone 1 F1
local_or_none_mht 3 A3 A4 A5 A1 A2 A6 B1 B2 B3 B4 B5 B6 B7 B8 B9 B10 B11 B12 
stopifnot(
  identical(alone_in("1", "systemic_mht"), cat_order(c("A1", "A2", "A6", b_oral, b_patch))),
  all(is.na(pg[approach == "1", includes2])),
  identical(alone_in("1", "tibolone"), "F1")
)

A1, A2, A6 and every B product are one level, systemic_mht. Tibolone is its own level. No rule of approach 1 reads a progestogen or a contraceptive. A woman on oestrogen with a separate progestogen is systemic_mht. A woman on a progestogen alone is not exposed.

Approach 2: route of the oestrogen 

knitr::kable(rule_table("2"))
variable rules alone pairs excludes
peroral_estrogen 12 A2 A6 B2 B3 B4 B5 B6 B8 B9 B10 B11 B12
tibolone 1 F1
transdermal_estrogen 3 A1 B1 B7
local_or_none_mht 3 A3 A4 A5 B1 B2 B3 B4 B5 B6 B7 B8 B9 B10 B11 B12 C1 C2 C3 C4 C5 D1 D2 D3 E1 I1 I2 
stopifnot(
  identical(alone_in("2", "transdermal_estrogen"), cat_order(c("A1", b_patch))),
  identical(alone_in("2", "peroral_estrogen"), cat_order(c("A2", "A6", b_oral))),
  all(is.na(pg[approach == "2", includes2])),
  identical(alone_in("2", "tibolone"), "F1")
)

Approach 2 splits systemic oestrogen by route. No rule reads injected oestrogen (A7), so it lights no route. The combined products follow the route of their oestrogen: the two patches, B1 and B7, are transdermal, and the ten tablets are peroral. Tibolone is again its own level.

Approach 3: the progestogen 

knitr::kable(rule_table("3"))
variable rules alone pairs excludes
estrogen_only 3 A1 A2 A6 B1 B2 B3 B4 B5 B6 B7 B8 B9 B10 B11 B12 C1 C2 C3 C4 C5 D1 D2 D3 E1 I1 I2
estrogen_progesterone_bioidentical 8 B4 B11 A1/A2/A6 + C1/C5
estrogen_progesterone_synthetic 37 B1 B2 B3 B5 B6 B7 B8 B9 B10 B12 A1/A2/A6 + C2/C3/C4/D1/D2/D3/E1/I1/I2
tibolone 1 F1 
bioidentical <- c("B4", "B11")
stopifnot(
  identical(alone_in("3", "estrogen_only"), c("A1", "A2", "A6")),
  identical(excludes_in("3", "estrogen_only"), paste(cat_order(c(b_oral, b_patch, partners_all)), collapse = " ")),
  identical(alone_in("3", "estrogen_progesterone_bioidentical"), bioidentical),
  identical(pair_in("3", "estrogen_progesterone_bioidentical", "includes1"), c("A1", "A2", "A6")),
  identical(pair_in("3", "estrogen_progesterone_bioidentical", "includes2"), c("C1", "C5")),
  identical(alone_in("3", "estrogen_progesterone_synthetic"), setdiff(cat_order(c(b_oral, b_patch)), bioidentical)),
  identical(pair_in("3", "estrogen_progesterone_synthetic", "includes2"), setdiff(partners_all, c("C1", "C5"))),
  identical(alone_in("3", "tibolone"), "F1")
)

Approach 3 splits systemic oestrogen by the progestogen taken with it. estrogen_only is A1, A2 or A6 with no combined product, no progestogen and no contraceptive in the same week. The two estrogen_progesterone levels split the progestogen. The codebook’s bioidentical level holds progesterone (C1), of every route the table gives it, and dydrogesterone (C5, and the combined products B4 and B11). Its synthetic level holds every other progestogen, including injected progesterone (C2), whether in a combined product or dispensed separately. The two names are the codebook’s labels. Tibolone is its own level. A progestogen or a contraceptive alone lights nothing.

Approach 3 also declares local_or_none_mht with an empty rule. That rule lights nothing.

Approach 4: route of the oestrogen by type of progestogen 

knitr::kable(rule_table("4"))
variable rules alone pairs excludes
estrogen_only 3 A1 A2 A6 B1 B2 B3 B4 B5 B6 B7 B8 B9 B10 B11 B12 C1 C2 C3 C4 C5 D1 D2 D3 E1 I1 I2
oral_estrogen_other_progestogen 24 B2 B3 B5 B6 B8 B9 B10 B12 A2/A6 + C3/C4/D1/D2/D3/E1/I1/I2
oral_estrogen_progesterone 6 B4 B11 A2/A6 + C1/C5
tibolone 1 F1
transdermal_estrogen_other_progestogen 10 B1 B7 A1 + C3/C4/D1/D2/D3/E1/I1/I2
transdermal_estrogen_progesterone 2 A1 + C1/C5 
four <- pg[approach == "4" & !is.na(includes1)]
progesterone <- pair_in("4", "oral_estrogen_progesterone", "includes2")
other_pg <- pair_in("4", "oral_estrogen_other_progestogen", "includes2")
stopifnot(
  identical(progesterone, c("C1", "C5")),
  identical(other_pg, setdiff(partners_all, c("C1", "C2", "C5"))),
  identical(pair_in("4", "transdermal_estrogen_progesterone", "includes2"), progesterone),
  identical(pair_in("4", "transdermal_estrogen_other_progestogen", "includes2"), other_pg),
  identical(pair_in("4", "oral_estrogen_progesterone", "includes1"), c("A2", "A6")),
  identical(pair_in("4", "oral_estrogen_other_progestogen", "includes1"), c("A2", "A6")),
  identical(pair_in("4", "transdermal_estrogen_progesterone", "includes1"), "A1"),
  identical(pair_in("4", "transdermal_estrogen_other_progestogen", "includes1"), "A1"),
  identical(alone_in("4", "oral_estrogen_progesterone"), bioidentical),
  identical(alone_in("4", "oral_estrogen_other_progestogen"), setdiff(b_oral, bioidentical)),
  identical(alone_in("4", "transdermal_estrogen_other_progestogen"), b_patch),
  length(alone_in("4", "transdermal_estrogen_progesterone")) == 0L,
  identical(alone_in("4", "estrogen_only"), c("A1", "A2", "A6")),
  identical(excludes_in("4", "estrogen_only"), excludes_in("3", "estrogen_only")),
  identical(alone_in("4", "tibolone"), "F1"),
  identical(pg[approach == "4" & is.na(includes1), variable], "local_or_none_mht"),
  identical(
    setdiff(cat_order(na.omit(pg[approach == "3", includes2])), c(progesterone, other_pg)),
    "C2"
  )
)

Approach 4 crosses the route of approach 2 with the progestogen of approach 3, with one difference: no approach 4 pair reads injected progesterone (C2). The chunk checks that difference against the approach 3 rules. Its levels:

  • oral_estrogen_progesterone: Femoston (B11) or Femostonconti (B4), the two oral combinations of dydrogesterone and oestrogen. Or an oral oestrogen (A2 or A6) with progesterone (C1) or dydrogesterone (C5).
  • oral_estrogen_other_progestogen: an oral combination product of any other category. Or A2 or A6 with an other progestogen.
  • transdermal_estrogen_progesterone: a transdermal oestrogen (A1) with C1 or C5.
  • transdermal_estrogen_other_progestogen: a transdermal combination product (B1 or B7), or A1 with an other progestogen.
  • estrogen_only: A1, A2 or A6, in a week with no category of the excludes column above.
  • tibolone: tibolone (F1).

Approach 4 declares local_or_none_mht with an empty rule, as approach 3 does. That rule lights nothing.

The progesterone levels read C1 and C5, dispensed separately or in B4 and B11. Every other progestogen that approach 4 pairs with an oestrogen is “other”. The table lists them from the two workbooks: the categories from the rules, and the routes and products from the product table.

knitr::kable(ptab[classification %in% other_pg, .(
  route = paste(unique(route), collapse = ", "),
  meaning = paste(unique(sub(" \\(.*\\)$", "", classification_meaning)), collapse = " | "),
  products = paste(unique(produkt_raw), collapse = ", ")
), keyby = .(category = classification)][match(other_pg, category)])

Approach 4 reads no rule that needs A3, A4, A5, A7, C2, G1 or H1. A week of these alone is local_or_none_mht. Injected progesterone (C2, Prolutex) is among the exclusions of estrogen_only and in no pair, so A1 with C2 lights no approach 4 level. Approach 3 reads the same week as estrogen_progesterone_synthetic.

The next table lists, for each category that approach 4 reads, its routes, its ATC codes, its products and the levels whose rules name it. The chunk checks the routes and the product categories that the prose above states.

read4 <- cat_order(c(four$includes1, na.omit(four$includes2)))
setdiff(legend$category, read4)

#> Duplicate column names found in molten data.table. Setting unique names using 'make.names'
in_rules <- in_rules[, .(levels = paste(unique(variable), collapse = ", ")), keyby = .(category = value)]

  route = paste(unique(route), collapse = ", "),
  atc = paste(sort(unique(atc)), collapse = " "),
  products = paste(unique(trimws(gsub("®", "", produkt_raw))), collapse = ", ")
), keyby = .(category = classification)][in_rules, on = "category"][match(read4, category)]

A separate progestogen lights an approach 4 level only in a week with an oestrogen. The chunk dispenses one product of each partner category alone, and then with Progynon (A2). Each supply covers weeks 1 to 8 or more, and the table shows the level in weeks 1 to 8.

partners <- data.table(
  produkt = c("Utrogestan", "Duphaston", "Cerazette", "Slinda", "Provera", "Depo-Provera", "Nexplanon", "Mirena"),
  fddd = c(56, 24, 12, 84, 12, 84, 84, 1),
  lnmn = c(UTROGESTAN, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA)
)
partners[, category := vapply(produkt, cat_of, "")]
stopifnot(all(partners$category %in% c(progesterone, other_pg)))
paired <- partners[, {
  alone <- run_toy(rx(produkt, 1, lnmn = lnmn, fddd = fddd))
  with_a2 <- run_toy(rbind(rx(produkt, 1, lnmn = lnmn, fddd = fddd), rx("Progynon", 1, 8)))
  stopifnot(all(alone[[category]][1:8]))
  .(alone = toString(unique(level_in(alone, 1:8))), with_progynon = toString(unique(level_in(with_a2, 1:8))))
}, by = .(produkt, category)]

  all(paired$alone == "local_or_none_mht"),
  identical(paired$with_progynon, fifelse(paired$category %in% progesterone,
    "oral_estrogen_progesterone", "oral_estrogen_other_progestogen"))
